<reason>CON won the motion as written: a coverage duty plus spending controls. PRO had the more memorable clinical/equity case, but never neutralized CON’s mechanism clash—scale, lifelong fills, and that brand-swapping is not an indication-level walk-away. CON’s pressure questions forced PRO to admit the duty can still bite near list; PRO’s two clips also cost execution. The diabetes analogy survived as fairness rhetoric, not as an actuarial answer.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s Q1/Q2 trap and R2 follow-through: if every maker prices “value” near list, coverage still binds, so outcomes language cannot replace the hard no of refusing the obesity indication itself.</best_rebuttal>
